question: Which statement reflects a basic aspect of cloud economics?
choices: Organizations can consume resources when needed and align spending more closely with usage
Organizations must purchase every server before determining actual demand
Cloud resources have the same cost regardless of consumption
Using the cloud removes the need to monitor costs
explanation: Cloud economics includes consuming resources on demand and aligning costs more closely with actual usage instead of purchasing all capacity in advance.

blueprint: Cost Savings of Moving to the Cloud
question: Which change can contribute to cost savings when an organization moves from an on-premises data center to AWS?
choices: Purchasing more unused hardware for future demand
Reducing expenses for operating and maintaining physical infrastructure
Increasing the time required to provision resources
Paying for maximum capacity at all times
explanation: Moving to AWS can reduce costs associated with purchasing, housing, powering, cooling, and maintaining physical infrastructure.

blueprint: Fixed Costs Compared with Variable Costs
question: Which example represents changing a fixed infrastructure cost into a variable cost?
choices: Buying a data-center building before deploying applications
Purchasing servers based on estimated demand for the next five years
Paying for AWS resources according to actual consumption
Signing a permanent maintenance contract for unused hardware
explanation: Usage-based AWS charges are variable costs because spending can change with consumption, unlike large fixed investments in facilities and hardware.

question: Which expense is commonly associated with operating an on-premises environment?
choices: Powering and cooling physical servers
Using an AWS edge location
Creating an IAM policy
Selecting an Amazon S3 storage class
explanation: On-premises environments commonly require spending for facilities, power, cooling, hardware, maintenance, and the personnel needed to operate physical infrastructure.

blueprint: Licensing Strategies > BYOL and Included Licenses
question: How does a Bring Your Own License model differ from an included-license model?
choices: BYOL uses an eligible license the customer already owns, while an included license is provided with the cloud offering
BYOL is available only for free software, while included licenses require customer-owned hardware
BYOL removes all software terms, while included licenses prohibit cloud use
BYOL always includes support from AWS, while included licenses never include software rights
explanation: With BYOL, a customer applies an eligible existing software license under its licensing terms. With an included-license offering, the software license cost and usage rights are included with the service or resource.

question: What is rightsizing in the AWS Cloud?
choices: Selecting resource types and sizes that match a workload's actual requirements
Deploying every workload on the largest available instance
Keeping unused resources running in case they are needed later
Moving every resource into the same Availability Zone
explanation: Rightsizing means matching resource configuration and capacity to workload needs so the organization can maintain performance without paying for unnecessary capacity.

question: Which economic benefit can automation provide in a cloud environment?
choices: It requires every change to be performed manually
It can reduce repetitive effort and apply processes consistently
It guarantees that resource usage never changes
It converts variable costs into permanent hardware expenses
explanation: Automation can reduce manual work, improve consistency, speed up repeatable operations, and help organizations manage cloud resources more efficiently.

question: How can AWS economies of scale benefit customers?
choices: AWS spreads infrastructure costs across a large customer base and can offer lower usage prices
Each customer must build a separate AWS Region
Customers are required to purchase all capacity years in advance
AWS prevents customers from reducing unused resources
explanation: AWS aggregates demand across many customers. This large scale can lower the cost of operating infrastructure and allow AWS to pass pricing efficiencies to customers.
